facts.raw_span: A 7-year-old boy presented with a 2-year history of progressive eruption of papules and nodules all over his body
The lesions did not cause pain or itching
The patient had no family history of cutaneous disorders
Multiple yellow to reddish brown firm papules and nodules were present on the scalp, face, neck, trunk, and limbs, including the axillae and inguinal regions
The nasal and oropharyngeal mucosa were also affected
The lesions were 2 to 10 mm in diameter with coalescing, yellow-brown nodules and plaques up to 4 cm in diameter on the face, trunk, and limbs
Routine laboratory test results and serum chemistry with serum lipid levels were within normal ranges
No clinical evidence of internal involvement was found on ultrasonography, computed tomography, or magnetic resonance imaging results
Dense diffuse cellular infiltrate composed mainly of foamy histiocytic cells and multinucleated Touton cells mixed with lymphocytes and eosinophils
Spindle cells and increased numbers of collagen fibers in a storiform arrangement were visible in the deep dermis
Positive for CD68 and CD163, but negative for S100, CD1a, and Langerin
